findings.title: Uncommitted ignore rules hide changed bytes from review and capture
findings.diagnosis: changedPaths applies worktree .gitignore files to untracked enumeration. It hashes the changed ignore file but omits the files that rule hides. Changing hidden from A to B preserves v7 identity. An existing independent review advances to VERIFICATION in both optional-binding forms. Pilot also appends two records after truncate changes hidden bytes. Committed-ignore exclusions remain a supported control.

evidence.observation: Four full transitions accepted changed hidden bytes: new/modified ignore rule, binding absent/present.
Mutating command returned success and appended two core records.

fix.action: Use ignore rules from the approved committed tree for untracked exclusion. Until that implementation exists, refuse snapshots whose added, modified or staged .gitignore could change the excluded set. Retire incomplete v7 dirty identities before accepting new reviews.
fix.why: Only committed ignore policy may exclude a file from this raw snapshot boundary. A changed rule must not silently widen the unobserved artifact.

verification.method: Run new/modified/nested ignore probes and pilot mutation with bindings absent/present.
verification.expected: Changed hidden bytes require a different artifact identity or an explicit refusal; no stale transition/evidence append.

verification.method: Replay actual stored v7 reviews that omitted hidden, including after removal of the rule; retain committed-ignore unchanged controls.
verification.expected: Incomplete predecessor reviews refuse; current unchanged supported artifacts pass.

fix.tradeoffs: Refusal temporarily narrows dirty-worktree support. Reading committed rules requires correct nested and negation semantics. Domain retirement requires fresh captures and reviews.
fix.alternative: Enumerate and bind all untracked files, including ignored files, under an explicitly approved scope policy. This changes build-output behavior and needs contract review.

findings.scope_qualification: C01 applies to paths hidden only by new or modified worktree ignore rules. It does not claim that files excluded by committed ignore policy must be captured. TODO later claims a broader ignored-file exclusion under Decision T; the human-approved scope artifact was not supplied. If that approval covers these newly hidden paths, reassess the finding rather than silently broadening the original closure criterion.

findings.title: Relative host store paths do not establish durable ancestry
findings.diagnosis: syncAncestors climbs the lexical store path. For relative-store/host/run it stops at dot. If the working directory has an existing unsynchronized ancestor entry, Append acknowledges while that entry can still disappear. The modeled crash recovers zero records without an error. Absolute-path controls preserve records.

evidence.observation: filepath.Dir reaches dot; the function returns without visiting absolute ancestors of cwd.
60 absolute-store crash images pass; seven recovery crash images pass.

fix.action: Normalize the host store to an absolute physical path before directory initialization and ancestry synchronization. Synchronize the resolved ancestry to the durable boundary, including any newly created suffix. Treat fsync errors as non-acknowledgment.
fix.why: Durability must hold for accepted relative paths and path aliases, not only absolute spellings.

verification.method: Run the relative-store crash probe, absolute control, symlink-to-store variants and same/different-run initialization.
verification.expected: Every acknowledged record remains recoverable in the modeled crash image.

verification.method: Inject fsync failure at every visited directory and interrupt recovery.
verification.expected: No failed sync acknowledges; recovery returns one verified prefix.

fix.tradeoffs: Path resolution can fail or race with host filesystem changes; those cases must refuse. Absolute conversion alone does not establish symlink-target ancestry.
fix.alternative: Refuse relative and unresolved/symlinked store roots until physical-ancestry synchronization is supported. This is smaller containment but breaks accepted relative-path usage.

findings.title: Review import accepts revoked route authority
findings.diagnosis: runHostReview locks the core and host chains but only calls EvaluateReview(history, review). It ignores the loaded core route state. After an approved same-unit, upstream-unit or whole-run Planning rewind, approvedCoreRouteDigest refuses, yet host review appends and returns CONTINUE_HMA_TRANSITION. The later coding gate still rejects the revoked route; this probe does not demonstrate stage advancement.

evidence.observation: Review callback discards core and only validates host-history review coherence.
All three rewinds still append the independent_review record.
Core-first revocation accepts a review append; terminal-first cases refuse.

fix.action: Within the locked review callback, resolve the named review dispatch and revalidate its unit route approval against the loaded core snapshot before appending.
fix.why: F02 explicitly requires review writes to refuse when revocation commits first; an atomic lock does not replace the missing authority predicate.

verification.method: Run ReviewAfterRewind and both-order CoreHostOrdering for review, unit/upstream/whole-run revocations and all five terminal outcomes.
verification.expected: Revocation-first returns route-approval refusal and preserves stored bytes. Host-first binds the pre-revocation core head.

verification.method: Run unchanged valid review import and the second coding gate.
verification.expected: Current authorized review remains usable; stale reviews cannot regain authority.

fix.tradeoffs: Historical results may need a separate nonauthorizing telemetry path if the product must retain them after revocation. Do not return an execution/progression action for such telemetry.
fix.alternative: Persist late reviews as explicitly nonauthorizing observations with no CONTINUE_HMA_TRANSITION action. This requires a separate documented record contract.

findings.title: Dependency invalidation has no verified plan graph
findings.diagnosis: approvedCoreRouteDigestIn clears every unit route after another unit returns to Planning or earlier. It does not load AcceptedPlanDigest, verify a graph or compute transitive dependents. In the U2->U1->U0 plus independent U3 scenario, all old routes are conservatively refused. A new trusted approval can restore U1 even when its plan digest names no resolved artifact. Safety containment exists, but B10/F05 plan-derived closure is incomplete.

evidence.observation: Source explicitly defers narrowing conservative invalidation with plan-derived dependents.
U0/U1/U2/U3 all refuse after U0 rewind; fresh-route approval with unresolved plan is accepted.
Pure engine consumes caller-supplied DependentUnitIDs; route replay has no verified graph input.

fix.action: Add a trusted host resolver for the accepted immutable plan digest. Validate unit IDs, dependencies and cycles. Compute the transitive affected set from that verified graph and apply it to route replay. Keep conservative refusal when resolution or validation fails.
fix.why: B10/F05 require plan-derived transitive invalidation and fail-closed behavior for missing or corrupt plans.

verification.method: Use a verified U2->U1->U0 graph and independent U3, then rewind U0.
verification.expected: Old U0/U1/U2 authority refuses; U3 may survive only when the verified graph proves independence.

verification.method: Remove/corrupt the plan, attempt review re-attestation, perform a whole-run rewind, then establish a fresh approved route with a verified current plan.
verification.expected: Missing/corrupt plans refuse. Review cannot revive invalidated authority. A fresh valid approval establishes new authority.

fix.tradeoffs: Graph persistence/resolution may need a scoped contract addition. Conservative refusal remains the safe containment while that work is approved.
fix.alternative: Retain whole-run conservative invalidation and explicitly obtain a human-approved change to the closure criterion. The auditor cannot change that criterion.

limitations: Isolation is partial. This is a fresh audit context with no implementer conversation. The initial source-bundle command read the whole named Gate A report and consolidation handoff instead of only closure fields and section 5. Those allowed files contain prior non-Gate-B assessments. Output was truncated. This prevents a claim of perfect fact-only blinding. No prohibited prior Gate B directory, Gate A v*.md handoff, claude directory or TODO Gate B claims was opened before this freeze.
Linux amd64, Go 1.27.1. No case-insensitive filesystem or non-Linux fsync/locking behavior was tested.
All executions used a copied target and scratch repositories/stores under this output directory. No network, real provider dispatch, model API or human production approval was exercised.

The durability model drops all unsynchronized directory entries and retains synchronized file bytes by inode. It covers 60 append and seven interrupted-recovery images, 20 reachable directory-fsync failure positions and 12-writer same/different-run tests. It is a model, not a physical power-loss test or exhaustive enumeration of every persistence subset.

The named old external helper scripts and the exact historical 40/55 process-exit checkpoints were not read or executed before Phase 1. Auditor-authored equivalent probes and current repository regressions were used. No historical review verdict is treated as proof.

Original-domain dirty replay probes construct v1-v6 framing for a regular untracked file; they do not execute every historical binary. Current schema separation, exact clean v1 construction and source inspection support the expiry result.

CI clean checkout capture is supported; dirty CI capture is deliberately refused. Hosted GitHub Actions, release closure, portable schema publication and full host-MVP conformance are outside this Gate B verdict.

Initial development probe logs contain corrected auditor fixture errors: uppercase enum literals in the first host probe and an omitted evidence-digest domain prefix in the first pilot probe. Final v3/race logs use corrected fixtures; the original logs remain available.

No approved Jev tool was exposed by the host. Advisory decisions used the auditor path. No worker dispatch was performed; the supplied liz/model/effort identity is coordinator metadata, not a runtime route attestation.
threat_model: Trusted host; accidents and drift; same-UID adversary out of scope

next_action.route: Use the human-approved Gate B implementer route; exact provider/model/effort is not in this audit packet. Perform the required exact-route hi before dispatch.
next_action.permission_envelope: Proposed bounded source/test remediation of C01-C04 in the cited snapshot, host-store and route-review paths; no commit, push, release or permission expansion is authorized by this audit.
next_action.approval_required: A fresh human-approved bounded remediation unit and eligible implementer/reviewer routes. This audit grants no approval.
next_action.stop_conditions: Stop if the fix widens scope, permissions or contract semantics; return to the human gate. Require fresh independent verification before claiming Gate B closure.
